en.summary: Light No Fire is Hello Games' next project after No Man's Sky, announced at The Game Awards 2023 by studio founder Sean Murray and still without a confirmed release date as of mid-2026. Unlike No Man's Sky's countless procedural galaxies, Light No Fire focuses on a single Earth-sized fantasy planet — roughly 197 million square miles by some estimates — that every player shares and explores together, combining survival, building, and RPG-style combat with swords, bows, and magic.

guideSections.title: One Shared Planet, Four Pillars
guideSections.description: Hello Games has described the project around four design pillars: a multiplayer Earth, a procedural Earth, a fantasy Earth, and an unexplored Earth. The whole planet streams together seamlessly — the studio has said players can sail across an ocean, dock a ship, and climb a mountain without a loading screen — and features persistent player-built settlements and communities.

guideSections.title: Learning from No Man's Sky's Launch
guideSections.description: After No Man's Sky's rocky 2016 debut following a long, hype-heavy marketing cycle, Hello Games has deliberately kept Light No Fire's public presence quiet, with only a small team confirmed to be working on it alongside the studio's ongoing No Man's Sky support. This makes a firm release window hard to pin down even this deep into development.
